prompt.context_jp: 夜の空気は冷え、閉じかけた店々の灯りだけ___街の輪郭を保っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 閉じかけた店々の灯りだけ___街の輪郭を保っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after だけ in this descriptive scene?

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが marks an exhaustive-listing subject: only the shops' lights (and nothing else) were preserving the town's outline. This is a classic context for が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は after だけ would weaken the exhaustive 'only X' nuance and sounds unnatural here; を would misread 灯り as an object.

prompt.context_jp: 待たされる時間はいつのまにか三十分を超え、湯呑みの茶___とうに冷めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 湯呑みの茶___とうに冷めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the tea in this descriptive line about Hiroshi waiting.

feedback.correct_en: The tea is a known, already-established referent being commented on — 'as for the tea, it had long gone cold.' This topic-comment structure takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame the cold tea as newly introduced information, which clashes with the narrator's reflective tone. を would make 茶 an object, which doesn't fit 冷めていた (intransitive).

contrast_examples.en: The tea has already gone cold (comment on known tea).
The tea's gone cold! (noticing it as news)

prompt.context_jp: 誰もいない部屋で、寛は待たされている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 壁の時計の秒針だけ___、律儀に時間を進めていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after 秒針だけ?

feedback.correct_en: 'Only the second hand' is exhaustively singled out as the one thing moving — a hallmark context for だけが.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would blur the 'only X and nothing else' emphasis; に would make 秒針 a location/target, breaking the sentence.

prompt.context_jp: 寛が売り込みの言葉を探している場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓の外では夜風___板塀を鳴らしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 夜風 in this scenic description.

feedback.correct_en: The night wind is newly introduced into the scene as the agent making the fence rattle — a neutral description takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 夜風 as a pre-established topic, which it isn't here; も ('also') has no comparable item in context.

contrast_examples.en: The wind is cold (commenting on known wind).

prompt.context_jp: 扉の向こうでハナが固まっている。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナ___目線をどこに置けばよいのか分からずに立ち尽くしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for ハナ as the main character being described.

feedback.correct_en: Hana is the established focal character; the narrator comments on her state. This long topic-comment sentence takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce her as new info, which misreads her role; に would mark a target/location.

prompt.context_jp: 扉を押すハナ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 金属のノブ___手のひらに冷たい。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle expressing her momentary sensation.

feedback.correct_en: This is a fresh sensory observation — the knob 'feels cold' as she touches it. Sensation/discovery sentences take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a general characterization of knobs; を doesn't fit the adjective predicate 冷たい.

prompt.context_jp: 航の裸を見てしまったハナ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頬に急速に血___上るのが、自分でも分かる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 血 (blood rushing to her cheeks).

feedback.correct_en: A spontaneous bodily event — the blood rushing up — is reported as new information with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame blood as a known topic being generalized about, which doesn't match this sudden sensation.

contrast_examples.en: As for tears, they won't stop (ongoing commentary).

prompt.context_jp: 歌っていたハナが足音に気づく瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 足音に気づいて、彼女の背筋___わずかに強張った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 背筋 (her back stiffening).

feedback.correct_en: An involuntary physical reaction is reported as a fresh event — が marks this subject of a spontaneous change.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would generalize about her back, which doesn't fit a single moment of tensing up.

prompt.context_jp: ママのいない店を去るハナ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰も見送りには出ていない朝の路地で、彼女___自分の靴音を数えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 彼女.

feedback.correct_en: 彼女 is the established protagonist of this paragraph; narration continues the topic with は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as newly identified in the scene, which contradicts the ongoing focus on Hana.

prompt.context_jp: 航の車の中、ハナの横顔が見える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 街灯の光___、規則正しくハナの横顔を舐めていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking 街灯の光.

feedback.correct_en: Fresh visual detail newly introduced into the scene; the streetlight light is the new subject acting on her profile — が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make streetlights a general topic, losing the vivid immediacy of the moment.

prompt.context_jp: 車内の会話が途切れた瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 信号___赤に変わり、車はゆるやかに停まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 信号.

feedback.correct_en: A change in the environment — the light turning red — is reported as a new event, so が. Notice how 車 later in the same sentence takes は: car is the established vehicle, the signal is the new happening.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the signal a known topic, losing the sense of 'the light (just) turned red.'

contrast_examples.en: The light is green (describing current state as topic).

prompt.context_jp: ハナが握手を求めて差し出した手を描写する一文。
prompt.prompt_jp: 差し出された手のひら___、街灯の光を受けてわずかに震えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 手のひら.

feedback.correct_en: The palm has just been introduced and is now being commented on with a descriptive observation — は fits the comment structure '(as for) the palm, it was trembling.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal a sudden discovery; here the narration pauses to describe the already-visible hand.

prompt.context_jp: 握手した瞬間の航の感覚。
prompt.prompt_jp: 握られた手のひら___、思っていたよりずっと小さかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 手のひら.

feedback.correct_en: The clasped palm is the topic being evaluated against an expectation ('smaller than he thought'). Comparison/evaluation comments take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as newly noticed existence, but the sentence is Kou's judgement about the hand, not a reveal.

prompt.context_jp: 寛がハナに頭を下げる朝の事務室。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナの背後で、ママの空席___わずかに揺れて見えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for ママの空席.

feedback.correct_en: Mama's empty seat is newly introduced into the scene as a quietly perceived image — が marks this subject of perception.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the empty seat as a prior topic, but it hasn't been raised yet in this paragraph.

contrast_examples.en: The empty seat came into view.

prompt.context_jp: ハナが角を曲がる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 角を曲がると、街の音___ふっと遠ざかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 街の音?

feedback.correct_en: A spontaneous change at the moment of turning the corner — the sounds suddenly recede. 〜と + sudden event takes が for the subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the city sounds into a general topic, erasing the suddenness.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアを開けると、風が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: When I opened the door, wind came in.

prompt.context_jp: 寛は応接室で待たされている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 寛はひとり革張りのソファに___を沈めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the body-part noun that collocates with 沈める here.

feedback.correct_en: 腰を沈める is the set collocation for sinking into a sofa/chair — one lowers one's hips/seat into it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 足を沈める suggests sinking feet into something; 頭を沈める isn't idiomatic for sitting.

prompt.context_jp: 老人が寛に感謝する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: ママちゃんのこと いろいろと ___を尽くしてくださって
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that forms a set phrase meaning 'did everything possible.'

feedback.correct_en: 手を尽くす is the fixed expression meaning 'to do everything one can / exhaust every means.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 足を尽くす and 目を尽くす aren't established idioms.

contrast_examples.jp: あらゆる手を尽くした。

contrast_examples.en: They did all they could to help.

prompt.context_jp: 航は染みを見て苛立つ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼は___打ちして、天井を仰いだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for the clicking-tongue gesture of annoyance.

feedback.correct_en: 舌打ち (tongue-click) is the standard expression for the 'tsk' sound of irritation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 歯打ち/口打ち aren't idiomatic ways to describe this reaction.

contrast_examples.en: I clicked my tongue in spite of myself.

prompt.context_jp: 売り込みに不慣れな寛。
prompt.prompt_jp: いかに商品の魅力を伝えるかで___がいっぱいだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the body-part word that forms the idiom 'preoccupied / mind full.'

feedback.correct_en: 頭がいっぱい means one's mind is completely occupied with something.
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸がいっぱい means emotionally overwhelmed (not preoccupied); 腹がいっぱい means physically full from eating.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事で頭がいっぱいだ。
contrast_examples.en: My mind is full of work.

contrast_examples.jp: 感動で胸がいっぱいだ。
contrast_examples.en: My heart is full with emotion.

prompt.context_jp: 翌朝、寛が改めて頭を下げる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 寛は姿勢を___、両手をそろえて頭を下げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb collocates with 姿勢?

feedback.correct_en: 姿勢を正す ('straighten one's posture / sit up properly') is the standard collocation for a formal, respectful bearing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 姿勢を開く isn't idiomatic; 姿勢を伸ばす is awkward — one says 背筋を伸ばす, not 姿勢を伸ばす.

contrast_examples.jp: 姿勢を正して話を聞く。

prompt.context_jp: ハナが不機嫌になる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナは眉根を___、窓の外へ視線を逃がした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 眉根 (brow).

feedback.correct_en: 眉をひそめる / 眉根をひそめる means 'to furrow one's brow' in displeasure or concern — the set collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 眉を伸ばす/広げる don't exist as idioms for this facial expression.

contrast_examples.jp: 不快感に眉をひそめた。

prompt.context_jp: 寛が自分の過ちを認める場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 匿名のショコラティエ様にも 人に言えないご事情が あると思います 私が___でした
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word Hiroshi uses to call himself out for his earlier judgment.

feedback.correct_en: 軽率 ('rash, thoughtless') is a standard self-criticism in a business apology — admitting he acted without proper consideration.
feedback.incorrect_en: 慎重 (cautious) and 丁寧 (polite/careful) are positive traits; apologizing by calling oneself 'cautious' makes no sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 軽率な発言を謝ります。
contrast_examples.en: I apologize for my thoughtless remark.

prompt.context_jp: ハナが差し出した手を握った航。
prompt.prompt_jp: 航は反射的に握り___、そして、自分の内側でなにかがひとつ、音もなく崩れ落ちるのを感じた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the compound verb ending for '(squeeze) back in return.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜返す on a verb means 'do back in response' — 握り返す = 'squeeze back.' That's exactly what happens here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 握り合い = 'grasp each other' loses the response nuance; 握り直す = 'regrip,' which isn't the point.

prompt.context_jp: 航がハナに秘密について語る場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for 'If it were easy to say, it wouldn't be a secret'?

choices.text: 簡単に答えられるぐらいなら それは秘密じゃないから
簡単に答えるぐらいなら それは秘密ないから

feedback.correct_en: The hypothetical 'if it's easy enough to be answered' uses the potential form 答えられる + ぐらいなら. 秘密じゃない is the correct negation of a noun.
feedback.incorrect_en: 答える (non-potential) loses the 'able to' nuance, and 秘密ない drops the required じゃ/では for noun negation.

contrast_examples.jp: 話せるぐらいなら悩まない。
contrast_examples.en: If I could just talk about it, I wouldn't be struggling.

prompt.context_jp: 航がハナにカバンを持ってくるよう頼む場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural in this urgent, slightly exasperated moment?

choices.text: カバンごと 持ってきてくれって 言ったじゃないですか
カバンまで 持ってきてくれって 言ったじゃないですか

feedback.correct_en: 〜ごと means 'the whole X / X and all,' which is exactly what Kou meant: bring the entire bag, not just one shirt.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜まで means 'even/as far as X,' which would imply the bag was an additional surprising item — wrong nuance here.

contrast_examples.jp: りんごを皮ごと食べる。
contrast_examples.en: Eat the apple skin and all.

prompt.context_jp: ハナが寛に、ママ本人の意向を伝える場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version matches Hana's polite reporting of what Mama said?

choices.text: ご本人が "誰にも知られたくない"と おっしゃられてたので
ご本人が "誰にも知られたくない"と 言ったので

feedback.correct_en: Hana uses honorific おっしゃる (+ progressive) to show respect to Mama when relaying her words to the young president — matching the polite workplace register.
feedback.incorrect_en: Plain 言った would be too blunt in this formal exchange with 社長 about a respected former colleague.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生がおっしゃっていました。

prompt.context_jp: ハナが航の涙を見て驚く場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for 'I didn't know tears could well up in an instant like that'?

choices.text: 涙って こんな一瞬で込み上げるんだ
涙って こんな一瞬で上がるんだ

feedback.correct_en: 涙が込み上げる is the set collocation for tears welling up from inside — it captures the sudden swell of emotion.
feedback.incorrect_en: 涙が上がる isn't idiomatic Japanese for tears welling up; it suggests tears literally rising, which isn't how Japanese expresses this.

contrast_examples.jp: 感情が込み上げてきた。

prompt.context_jp: 寛が老人の感謝に応えて謙遜する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which humble deflection sounds more natural for the young president?

choices.text: 私が特別 努力したというわけではなく 会社として当たり前のことをした
私が特別 努力しなかったので 会社として当たり前のことをした

feedback.correct_en: 〜というわけではなく softens the denial: 'it's not that I made any special effort.' This is standard humble/polite deflection.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜しなかったので flatly states 'because I didn't make a special effort,' which sounds awkward and almost self-dismissive rather than modest.

contrast_examples.jp: 嫌いというわけではない。
contrast_examples.en: It's not that I dislike it.
I don't go because I dislike it.
